vision.purpose: Age of Empires IV. Read the resource panel (food, wood, gold, stone stockpiles; in the default layout it is at the bottom left, next to the number of workers on each), the population as current/maximum, the idle villager count if a number is shown, the total villagers (the worker counts beside each resource plus idle, only if all are readable), the current age (Dark, Feudal, Castle or Imperial; the age shown, not one being built), and the in-game clock. Report only numbers you can actually read. Report phase 'match_end' on a victory/defeat banner or the post-game summary, and 'menu' in menus, lobbies or loading screens. When the player's army is fighting on screen, report a fight event with what the frame shows: the trend, where it is, the matchup, numbers, whether ranged units are screened, Mangonel splash, enemy siege and how reinforcements arrive; give unknown for anything unclear. Read the map name and the opponent's civilisation from the loading screen. When enemy buildings or units are visible (scouting, fights, their base), list them with the roster's exact names and counts; never list anything in the fog of war.

attributes.description: How the fight looks now: more of the player's units left with healthy bars (winning), fewer or dying faster (losing).
Where it is: within reach of an enemy Town Center, Keep or tower; of the player's own; open ground; a narrow gap between obstacles; a sacred site.
Do the player's main units counter the enemy's main units (spears vs cavalry, archers vs spears, horsemen vs archers or siege, crossbows vs heavy), the reverse, or neither?
The player's visible army against the visible enemy army, by rough size.
The player's ranged units behind their melee (screened), in front of it or alone (exposed), or none.
Whether enemy Mangonels or similar are firing, and if so whether the player's units are in a tight clump or spread out.
Enemy siege present and nobody of the player's attacking it (ignored), being attacked, or none.
Reinforcements arriving as a group, or single units walking in one by one.

concepts.title: Keep villagers coming
concepts.summary: Continuous villager production from the Town Center is the backbone of the economy. Every gap of 20 seconds is one villager you will never get back.
good: Queue villagers without gaps
Rally new villagers straight onto a resource
bad: Town Center standing idle
Losing production while housed

concepts.title: Build houses before the cap
concepts.summary: Reaching the population cap stops all production. A house adds 10 population (5 for the Malians, who build them for half the cost; the Mongols need none).
good: Start a house a few population before the cap
bad: Hitting the cap and only then building

concepts.title: Age up on time, with the economy behind it
concepts.summary: You age up by building a landmark. Hitting your target time matters, but aging with too few villagers leaves you weak in the next age.
good: Plan the landmark and its villagers early
Keep producing villagers while the landmark builds
bad: Pulling every villager off resources to build
Aging with a thin economy

concepts.title: Spend what you gather
concepts.summary: Unspent resources do nothing. A large bank usually means a missing production building, upgrade or Town Center.
good: Add production when resources pile up
Research economy upgrades
bad: Thousands banked mid-game

concepts.title: Scout, then react
concepts.summary: Knowing what the opponent is building lets you choose the right units and defences instead of guessing.
good: Scout early and again at each age-up
Build counter units to what you saw
bad: Massing one unit type without scouting

concepts.title: Advice depends on the game in front of you
concepts.summary: The same fight needs different advice by civilisation (unique units and missing Blacksmith upgrades change the numbers), map (open maps favour pressure, closed maps favour booming and late siege fights), age (Feudal fights are about economic damage and +1 upgrades, Castle fights about unit tiers and siege, Imperial fights about value per population), what was scouted, team or 1v1, and skill level (one fix at a time below Platinum; micro such as kiting and charge recycling above it). Never assume what was not on the player's screen, and say which patch a number comes from.
good: Naming the civilisations, map and age before advising on a fight
Giving a lower-rated player one fix at a time
bad: Applying generic unit numbers to a unique unit
Advising on enemy units or resources that were never on screen

prohibitedAdvice: Anything about the opponent that is not visible on the player's own screen (fog of war, hidden armies)
Exploits, bugs or tools against the game's rules

terminology.housed: at the population cap, unable to make units
terminology.floating: holding a large unspent bank of resources

playbook.title: Never stop villager production
playbook.principle: Every second a Town Center is idle is a villager you never get back, and the loss compounds. Guides and coaches name macro as the biggest gap between Gold or Platinum and Diamond players.
good: One or two villagers queued at every check
Production carries on through age-ups and fights
bad: Town Center idle while you place buildings or fight
Five villagers queued, locking resources
signals: Villager count behind the one-Town-Center curve (21 at 5:00, 36 at 10:00)
Total villagers flat between checks
playbook.fix: Queue one or two villagers every time you check a Town Center, never more than three.

sources.title: How many villagers should you make, GamerBlurb

playbook.drill: Against the AI, play one Town Center with one goal: 36 villagers at 10:00.

playbook.title: Zero idle villagers
playbook.principle: Idle villagers are invisible lost income, usually after a resource runs dry, a building finishes or a raid.
good: Idle icon at zero most of the time
Idle villagers back to work within about 10 seconds
bad: Builders left idle after a house
Villagers still garrisoned long after a raid
signals: Idle villager count above zero for more than 15 seconds
playbook.fix: Bind select idle villager to an easy key and press it after every build and every fight.

sources.title: Age of Empires IV hotkeys (Xbox Wire)

playbook.title: Build houses ahead of time
playbook.principle: Hitting the population cap stops every production queue at once. Houses are cheap insurance.
good: Cap 5 to 15 above your population
Two houses at a time from late Feudal
bad: Population at cap for 20 seconds or more
Starting a house only after hitting the cap
signals: Population equal to the cap while queues are full
playbook.fix: Start a house when you are within 5 of the cap, within 10 once you have two Town Centers.

playbook.title: Hit your opening's Feudal timing
playbook.principle: A build order is a timing contract. Missing it by 30 seconds or more means the economy leaked somewhere.
good: Feudal within 15 seconds of the build target
Villager split matching the build
bad: Feudal at 6:00 or later on a standard build
Gold or wood never set up
signals: Age icon changes late; food reached 400 but gold sat below 200
playbook.fix: Pick one build per civilisation and play it against the AI until you land within 15 seconds three times in a row.

sources.title: Abbasid two Town Center build, aoeinfo
Opening builds by civilisation, Guild Order

playbook.drill: Run the opening 20 or more times against the AI, then review the replay.

playbook.title: Fast castle needs a payoff and safety
playbook.principle: A fast castle (about 7:30 to 9:30) buys strong units and techs but leaves you exposed in Feudal. It works when you scouted no early aggression or can hold it cheaply.
good: A planned unit or tech spike after Castle
Spearmen or a tower if Feudal pressure was scouted
bad: Clicking Castle with no production planned
Fast castle into a scouted early stable with no spears
signals: Little or no army near 8:00 while enemy units show on the minimap
playbook.fix: Before clicking Castle, decide your first two units or techs, and add spears if you saw a stable.

sources.title: Castle units vs Feudal units thread, official forums
Abbasid two Town Center build, aoeinfo

playbook.title: Expand when it is safe
playbook.principle: A second Town Center is the strongest economic investment, but against early pressure the wood is better spent on army. In Update 17.0 a Town Center takes 165 seconds to build.
good: Second Town Center around 5:00 to 5:40 after scouting no early military
A third once you control the map
bad: Never expanding when not under pressure
Two Town Centers into a scouted rush
signals: One Town Center past 12:00; villagers well below the strong-player curve
playbook.fix: If your scout at about 4:30 shows no military buildings, start a second Town Center before 6:00.

sources.title: Abbasid two Town Center build, aoeinfo
One vs two Town Centers, Steam discussions

playbook.title: Match villagers to what you spend
playbook.principle: Your villager split should follow your unit and tech plan. Gold-heavy units such as knights and men-at-arms need far more on gold.
good: About 40% on gold for a gold-heavy army
More on wood while expanding and farming
bad: 25 on food and 3 on gold while making knights
Mining stone with no plan for it
signals: One resource climbing for two minutes while another sits near zero
playbook.fix: Every minute, move three to five villagers from the biggest bank to the smallest.

playbook.title: Spend down your banks
playbook.principle: Unspent resources are an army you do not have. A bank of 1,000 or more of one resource usually means a missed timing.
good: Under about 500 of each resource outside planned saves
Production added as income grows
bad: 1,000 or more banked
1,500 food with idle production
signals: A resource above 1,000 for a minute or more
playbook.fix: Add a production building or a tech, sell at the market, or move villagers off that resource.

playbook.title: Move to farms before food runs dry
playbook.principle: Sheep, berries and deer near the Town Center run out in Feudal. A late switch to farms means idle villagers and a food crash; farms near the Town Center are also safe from raids.
good: Farms built as each early food source empties
Horticulture researched (+10% food gathering)
bad: Villagers walking to far deer under raid pressure
Many idle villagers when the sheep run out
signals: Idle spike and flat food around 6 to 10 minutes
playbook.fix: Bank wood for farms one or two minutes before sheep and berries run out.

sources.title: Early economy, Age of Empires wiki

playbook.title: The early scout pays twice
playbook.principle: The scout brings sheep home for food, then finds information. With Professional Scouts it can carry carcasses, moving 55% slower while carrying.
good: Sheep pushed to the Town Center early
Enemy gold and military buildings checked
bad: Scout idle at home
Scout lost to the enemy Town Center
signals: No fog cleared in the enemy half by 3:00
playbook.fix: Scout path: sheep, then enemy gold and production, then home.

sources.title: Early economy, Age of Empires wiki

playbook.title: Scout what changes your decisions
playbook.principle: The enemy's age-up landmark, military buildings, second Town Center and blacksmith decide your next three minutes. Scout before committing and before every age-up.
good: Checks at 2 to 3 minutes, at enemy Feudal, then every 2 to 3 minutes
Units or outposts on attack paths
bad: Learning the enemy army only when it arrives
signals: No friendly units in enemy territory for three minutes or more
playbook.fix: Put a scout, horseman or outpost on the attack paths and check the enemy base at each timing.

playbook.title: Build counters before the threat arrives
playbook.principle: Age of Empires IV runs on counters: spears beat cavalry, archers beat spears and light infantry, horsemen beat ranged units and siege, crossbows and handcannons beat men-at-arms and knights, mangonels punish massed ranged units, springalds beat siege.
good: Composition changed within one production cycle of scouting
bad: Archers into men-at-arms
Knights into spears
signals: Lopsided losses after a fight
playbook.fix: Name the enemy's main unit and queue its counter.
playbook.why: Bonus damage drives the counters: Archers get +5 to +8 against light melee, Crossbows +10 to +12 against heavy units, Horsemen about +10 against ranged units and siege, and Spearmen brace against cavalry charges. Armor subtracts from both base and bonus damage, so the right unit can deal several times the damage of the wrong one (wiki values).

playbook.title: Upgrades are army supply
playbook.principle: A +1 upgrade multiplies every unit of that line, and armies that skip upgrades lose even trades.
good: First upgrade for your main line once you commit to it
Upgrades matched to the opponent
bad: A 20-minute game with no blacksmith
Upgrading a line you then abandon
signals: Gold floating while the army fights
playbook.fix: Build a blacksmith as Feudal completes and research +1 for your main unit line.
playbook.why: One point of armor matters most when attack is low against armor: an archer doing 3 damage against 2 armor does 2 once the target gets +1, a third less. Steeled Arrow costs 50 wood and 125 gold (wiki).

playbook.title: Park the army between the threat and your economy
playbook.principle: Keep the army on the enemy's likely path to your exposed gold and wood, close enough to your defences to fall back.
good: Army at the forward gold, a chokepoint or a sacred site
Reinforcements rallied there
bad: Army idle in base while forward villagers die
Army deep in enemy land for no reason
signals: Enemy units at your resources while your army is far away
playbook.fix: Rally production to a forward position and park the army there between attacks.

playbook.title: Attack with a goal and an exit
playbook.principle: Attack a specific resource or objective, and retreat from fights you are losing instead of trading everything.
good: Raid, kill villagers, leave before the counter-army arrives
Fighting with a numbers or upgrade edge
bad: Chasing a fleeing army under their Town Center
Fighting at a supply disadvantage
signals: Your army supply dropping sharply near enemy buildings
playbook.fix: Before you move out, decide the target and when you will leave.

playbook.title: Do not fight under enemy Town Centers, towers or keeps
playbook.principle: Defensive buildings add free damage, and garrisoned villagers add arrows. Lure the army out, or bring siege.
good: Disengaging when the enemy runs under their Town Center
Rams or a bombard before engaging a keep
bad: Attack-moving into a keep
Diving a Town Center with archers
signals: Your army fighting inside enemy building range while your population drops
playbook.fix: Stop at the edge of building range and pull back unless you have siege.

sources.title: Town Center, Age of Empires wiki

playbook.why: A Town Center gains one arrow per garrisoned unit up to about eight, reaching 6 tiles (7 with Arrowslits), and a Keep fires a three-arrow volley plus one per garrisoned unit at 8 tiles (wiki values). Those arrows are free damage for the defender, on top of their reinforcements being seconds away.

playbook.title: Defend on your terms at home
playbook.principle: When outnumbered, fight under your Town Center, towers or keep. Garrisoned villagers add arrows, but ringing everyone in for minutes costs economy.
good: Pulling back to your defences
Garrisoning only villagers in danger
bad: Meeting a bigger army in the open
All villagers garrisoned for minutes
signals: Many idle or garrisoned villagers for more than 30 seconds
playbook.fix: Retreat to your defences, then send villagers back to work the moment the threat leaves.

sources.title: Age of Empires IV hotkeys (Xbox Wire)
Town Center, Age of Empires wiki

playbook.why: Each villager garrisoned in a Town Center adds an arrow, so a full Town Center hits much harder, but every garrisoned villager gathers nothing: 20 villagers inside for 30 seconds is 10 villager-minutes of lost work.

playbook.title: Protect villagers cheaply
playbook.principle: Raids win through idle and dead villagers, not building damage. Outposts, a few spears and a quick reaction beat full garrisons.
good: Outposts or towers at the forward gold
A small home guard near exposed resources
bad: Losing five or more villagers to four horsemen
Garrisoning everything for one horseman
signals: Villager count dropping while production is running
playbook.fix: Build an outpost at every resource line away from the Town Center and keep a small home guard.

sources.title: Town Center, Age of Empires wiki

playbook.why: A dead villager costs 50 food plus all its future gathering, and villagers forced into a Town Center gather nothing while inside, so raids hurt through lost time even without kills. Secondary Town Centers do not shoot unless garrisoned.

playbook.title: Shape the fight
playbook.principle: A wider front lets more of your units fight. Fight bigger armies at chokepoints, and spread ranged units against mangonels.
good: Ranged units behind spears
Spread formation against mangonels
Engaging from two angles
bad: A single line through a choke into a concave
Clumped archers under mangonel fire
signals: Heavy losses in a fight at a choke
playbook.fix: Spread out before engaging and approach from two angles.
playbook.why: Only units that can reach the enemy deal damage: a wide front lets more of your units fight at once, and a narrow choke lets fewer of theirs fight. A flank also reaches their ranged units and siege, where Horsemen get bonus damage.

playbook.title: Siege with an escort and a purpose
playbook.principle: Rams are for buildings and die to melee units. Mangonels punish clumps. Springalds counter siege. Cavalry is the best answer to siege.
good: Mangonels aimed at the middle of clumps, then pulled back
Rams escorted by spears and archers
bad: Unescorted mangonels
Siege attack-moved into a cavalry army
signals: Siege ahead of your army on the minimap
playbook.fix: Keep siege behind the front line with an escort assigned.
playbook.why: Siege resists arrows by percentage (Mangonel about 85%, Ram about 95%) and takes extra melee damage, so only melee and cavalry kill it quickly. Update 17.0 raises Ram health from 370 to 410.

playbook.title: Sacred sites: gold and a win condition
playbook.principle: A held sacred site gives gold, and holding all of them starts a victory timer that forces the opponent to move out.
good: Monks escorted by a squad
Contesting the opponent's countdown
bad: Ignoring the timer
Unescorted monks
signals: The sacred site countdown on screen
playbook.fix: Escort the monk and leave a squad at captured sites.

playbook.title: Choose boom or pressure from the scout
playbook.principle: Boom when the opponent is passive; pressure punishes greedy builds in Feudal. Turn successful pressure into an expansion or an age-up.
good: Aggression that does damage and buys a safe expansion
Booming behind cheap defence
bad: Aggression with no damage and no expansion
Booming blind into a scouted rush
signals: Army supply high while villagers stay flat
playbook.fix: After each attack, turn the advantage into a Town Center or an age-up.

playbook.title: Grow production with income
playbook.principle: More income needs more production buildings, or the resources float.
good: Production buildings added as income grows
Queues kept running
bad: 80 villagers and one barracks

playbook.title: Control groups and hotkeys
playbook.principle: Speed comes from keyboard habits, not from clicking faster.
good: All Town Centers on one key, cycled
Army on a control group
Idle villager key within easy reach (VortiX)
bad: Clicking the Town Center on screen
No control groups
signals: Slow reactions to idle villagers or raids
playbook.fix: Set keys for your Town Centers, army and idle villagers before your next ranked game.

playbook.title: Run a macro loop
playbook.principle: A fixed check loop stops things being forgotten: Town Center queues, idle villagers, houses, banks, minimap.
good: A check every 30 seconds or so
bad: Watching the army for two minutes straight
signals: Gaps in villager production during fights
playbook.fix: Before each army command, tap your Town Center key and queue a villager.

playbook.title: Practise builds against the AI, then review
playbook.principle: Repeat an opening 20 or more times against the AI, then review replays for leaks. The AI is for macro practice, not strategy practice.
good: Two or three openings per civilisation with timings written down
bad: Learning builds in ranked
signals: Feudal time varying a lot between games
playbook.fix: Play five games against the AI for every new build before taking it to ranked.

playbook.title: Take even fights only with the upgrade edge
playbook.principle: With equal numbers, the side one Blacksmith upgrade or unit tier ahead usually wins, so time even fights to your upgrades, not theirs.
playbook.why: Damage per hit is attack plus bonus minus the target's armor, with a floor of 1, and armor also reduces bonus damage. One point matters most when attack is low against armor: an archer doing 3 damage against 2 ranged armor does 2 once the target gets +1, a third less (wiki and Steam guide; patch values vary). Steeled Arrow costs 50 wood and 125 gold in Feudal; Veteran tiers cost 100 food and 250 gold.
good: Two Blacksmith upgrades done before attacking a same-size army that has none
The Blacksmith kept researching while you mass units
bad: Forcing a fight 20 seconds before your own +1 finishes
Base units into Veteran units at equal numbers
signals: Even-sized fights lost with no clear counter or position problem
playbook.fix: Delay an even fight until your pending upgrade or tier finishes.

Unit upgrades, Age of Empires wiki

playbook.drill: Custom game or combat simulator: 15 against 15 with and without +1 armor, and count the survivors.

playbook.title: Fight in your power window, not theirs
playbook.principle: Hit the opponent while their resources are tied up in an age-up landmark, a Town Center or a Keep, and avoid big fights just before your own age-up or tier lands.
playbook.why: Resources spent on a landmark or Town Center are not units, so the army in front of you is smaller than their economy suggests. In Update 17.0 a Town Center takes 165 seconds instead of 150, so an expanding player is exposed for longer. Once Castle Age lands, new tiers, Springalds, Mangonels and armor techs can flip the same matchup.
good: Hitting a scouted landmark under construction with Feudal units before their Castle units arrive
bad: Losing the whole Feudal army to an opponent who just reached Castle Age
signals: Fights lost shortly after the opponent aged up
playbook.fix: Check the enemy's age-up before committing, and attack into their age-up rather than after it.

playbook.title: Judge a fight by the resources traded, not the kill count
playbook.principle: Count what died in resources and position, not in heads.
playbook.why: Unit costs differ by up to four times: a Spearman is 60 food and 20 wood, an Archer 30 food and 50 wood, a Knight 140 food and 100 gold, a Mangonel 400 wood and 200 gold. Losing 5 Knights (1,200) to kill 12 Archers (960) is a losing trade despite winning 12 to 5, and one Mangonel is worth more than seven Archers. The in-game military score weights losses heavily, so it does not tell you who won the fights.
good: Losing 8 Spearmen to kill 2 Mangonels and 4 Archers
bad: Chasing Archers with Knights into a Spearman wall for "10 kills"
signals: Army size falling more than the enemy's visible army
playbook.fix: Count each fight's losses in resources before deciding who won.

playbook.title: Reinforce as a group, never one by one
playbook.principle: Rally new units to a safe point behind the army and send them in together.
playbook.why: In ranged fights, strength grows faster than numbers: ten units arriving together beat two groups of five arriving one after the other by much more than double (general RTS reasoning, not measured for AoE4). Units walking in alone also arrive without a concave and die before they contribute. The official tips say to move rally points to a staging point before a fight.
good: Production rallied beside the army, new groups sent in every 30 to 40 seconds
bad: The rally flag in the enemy base, a line of single Spearmen across the map
signals: Single units arriving at a fight; small groups dying away from the main army
playbook.fix: Move your rally point behind your army and send reinforcements in batches.

sources.title: Tips to get your army up to speed (Xbox Wire)
Things I struggle with in AoE4, Steam discussions

playbook.title: Make an even army come to you
playbook.principle: When the armies are close in size, fight near your own Town Center, towers and production.
playbook.why: Your reinforcements walk 10 to 20 seconds, theirs a minute or more; your Town Center and towers add arrows; villagers can repair or attack rams; and your damaged units can retreat to heal. The attacker must win by a margin to make up the walk.
good: Taking the fight a few tiles in front of your own Town Center
bad: Chasing a retreating army across the map into their Town Center range
signals: Fights won near your own buildings and lost far from them
playbook.fix: With even armies, hold near your production until the enemy commits, then engage.

sources.title: 5 defense tips every AoE4 player needs (video)

playbook.title: Retreat while the fight is only slightly lost
playbook.principle: Pull back as soon as the trade turns against you, not when three units are left, and heal before the next fight.
playbook.why: Units deal full damage at low health, but a losing army that stays gives the winner free hits, and fleeing infantry is caught by faster cavalry. Pulling back early saves most of the army's value. Monks heal about 7 health per second (half in combat), so a healed army gains a free army's worth of health over several fights (wiki numbers).
good: Pulling back to a Town Center halfway through a losing fight, healing, and returning at full health
bad: Attack-moving until the army is wiped
Infantry retreating from Horsemen in the open
signals: Lost fights where the army fell to under a quarter of its size
playbook.fix: Pull back toward your Town Center or towers the moment you are losing the trade.

playbook.title: Focus the units they cannot afford to lose
playbook.principle: Ranged units on light infantry, Horsemen on archers and siege, Spearmen on cavalry, melee and cavalry on Mangonels and Springalds, melee and villagers on rams.
playbook.why: Bonus damage is large: Archers get +5 to +8 against light melee, Crossbows +10 to +12 against heavy units, Horsemen about +10 against ranged units and siege. Siege resists arrows by percentage (Mangonel about 85%, Ram about 95%) and takes extra melee damage, so arrows barely scratch it while melee shreds it (wiki values, patch-dependent).
good: Knights diving the Mangonel
Archers told to shoot the Spearmen, not the Men-at-Arms
bad: Thirty Archers shooting a Ram
Horsemen attacking Spearmen
signals: An enemy Mangonel still firing after ten seconds of fighting; your ranged units shooting siege
playbook.fix: Send your cavalry at their siege and ranged units, and point your ranged units at their light infantry.

sources.title: Attack-move or focus fire, official forums

playbook.title: Keep ranged units behind a melee screen
playbook.principle: Kite slow melee units with ranged units; against cavalry, pull the ranged units behind your Spearmen instead of trying to outrun them.
playbook.why: Archers have 5 tiles of range and fire about every 1.6 seconds, so a step back between shots costs nothing against slow Men-at-Arms. Horsemen are faster than Archers, so kiting them fails; the counter is to run into your own Spearmen and fight from behind them.
good: Archers stepping back after each volley
Archers falling back behind braced Spearmen when Horsemen come
bad: Archers standing still while melee closes
Archers alone in the open with Horsemen on them
signals: Your ranged units in front of your melee, or in melee contact
playbook.fix: Keep your ranged units on their own control group behind your melee and step them back between volleys.

sources.title: How to micro in AoE4, DiamondLobby

playbook.drill: Custom game: kite 10 Archers against 6 Men-at-Arms without losing one.

playbook.title: Spread out or dive against Mangonels
playbook.principle: Never leave massed ranged units clumped in Mangonel range: spread them, or kill the Mangonel with cavalry inside its minimum range.
playbook.why: A Mangonel fires three projectiles into a small area with 9 tiles of range and a 3-tile minimum range, has about 130 health and resists 85% of arrow damage. Clumped units take every projectile; spread units take one. Formations loosen as units re-clump in combat, so re-spread every few seconds (wiki and forum).
good: Archers in a loose line
Three Horsemen running past the screen to the Mangonel
bad: Twenty-five Archers in one ball losing six to one volley
signals: Several of your health bars dropping at once; an enemy Mangonel nobody attacks
playbook.fix: Spread your ranged units and send cavalry straight at the Mangonel.

sources.title: Do you find mangonels OP, official forums

playbook.title: Spearmen must stand or attack-move to brace
playbook.principle: Spearmen brace against cavalry only when idle or attack-moving; cavalry must pull out and re-engage to charge again.
playbook.why: A Knight's charge hits for 32 to 45 against 21 to 30 for a normal hit. Braced Spearmen cancel the charge and stop the cavalry, but only when idle or attack-moving, not on a move command and not when hit from behind. A forum rule of thumb says Spearmen need about two to one against Lancers, depending on upgrades.
good: Spearmen holding position as Knights charge in
Knights hitting, pulling back three tiles and charging again
bad: Right-click moving Spearmen into Knights
Knights stuck in a long melee with Spearmen
signals: Spearmen walking, not fighting, when cavalry hits them
playbook.fix: Attack-move or stop your Spearmen as cavalry approach, and pull your cavalry out to charge again.

playbook.title: Attack-move into fights, then target what matters
playbook.principle: Attack-move for the first contact, then give targeted orders for priority units.
playbook.why: Attack-move makes units fight whatever is nearest, which suits the opening contact and big ranged groups; targeted orders kill priority units but can overkill or make units walk past screens. Before 17.0, attack-move could pull units onto buildings mid-fight; Update 17.0 adds a setting so attack-move ignores buildings, while rams, trebuchets and cannons still target them. The coach cannot see this setting.
good: Attack-moving the army in, then sending cavalry at the siege
bad: Units hitting a house while their army dies next to them
signals: Your units attacking walls, houses or farms while enemy units are in range
playbook.fix: If your army keeps hitting houses in fights, turn on the 17.0 setting so attack-move ignores buildings.

playbook.title: Siege fights decide Castle and Imperial games
playbook.principle: Escort your siege with units that beat the enemy's siege-killers, and kill their siege before anything else.
playbook.why: Siege is expensive and takes a lot of population: a Mangonel is 400 wood and 200 gold. Springalds are the anti-siege tool. Rams resist arrows almost entirely and take extra melee damage; Update 17.0 raises Ram health from 370 to 410, so a melee response that used to just kill a ram now leaves it alive.
good: Springalds behind Spearmen killing both enemy Mangonels before they fire twice
bad: Mangonels walking ahead of the army and dying to four Horsemen
signals: Your siege ahead of your army; rams at a building with none of your melee near them
playbook.fix: Keep your siege behind your melee and kill the enemy's siege first.

playbook.title: Know how far the arrows reach before choosing where to fight
playbook.principle: Fight outside enemy arrow range and lure the enemy inside yours.
playbook.why: Each unit garrisoned in a Town Center adds an arrow, up to about eight, reaching 6 tiles (7 with Arrowslits); the capital Town Center has a stronger extra arrow. Secondary Town Centers only shoot when garrisoned. A Keep fires a three-arrow volley plus one per garrisoned unit at 8 tiles (wiki values, check after 17.0).
good: Fighting at least 9 tiles away from an enemy Keep
bad: Chasing into an expansion Town Center full of villagers
signals: Fights in frame with an enemy Town Center, Keep or tower
playbook.fix: Pull the fight at least 9 tiles away from enemy Town Centers and Keeps before engaging.

sources.title: Town Center, Age of Empires wiki

playbook.title: Defend or trade bases: compare speed and win conditions
playbook.principle: Trade bases only if your army is faster, their base is weaker, and you win the race to their landmarks or production; otherwise go home.
playbook.why: Age of Empires IV is won by destroying landmarks (or by a Wonder or sacred sites), and landmarks take a long time to break without siege. If your army destroys their production faster than theirs destroys yours, the trade is yours.
good: Knights against slow infantry, killing military buildings while Town Center arrows hold home
bad: Slow infantry with no rams in their base while 30 Knights burn your villagers
signals: Both armies in each other's base; under-attack alerts at home
playbook.fix: Before trading bases, check that your army breaks their buildings faster than theirs breaks yours.

playbook.title: At max population, value per population wins
playbook.principle: Near 200 population, upgraded gold units beat cheap units; before that, cost efficiency matters more.
playbook.why: The population cap is 200, Knights take 1 population and siege about 3 (forum figures). Once both sides are maxed, the stronger army per population slot wins, so replace cheap units with upgraded ones instead of adding more.
good: Swapping cheap units for upgraded gold units at 200 population
bad: Throwing more cheap units at an upgraded army at max population
signals: Population at the cap and fights still lost
playbook.fix: At max population, replace cheap units with upgraded gold units.

units.name: Villager
units.why: Rams have 95% ranged resistance but take full melee damage, so a villager pull kills Feudal rams. Villagers are unarmored (50 HP); horsemen and archers kill them fast, so raids need spearmen/TC garrison.
units.look: Unarmored civilian carrying tools/resources; no shield or helmet. English/Lancaster villagers hold a bow.

units.name: Scout
units.why: Only 1 base damage, so any real military beats it (and it is useless vs monks/villagers). The +10 vs siege bonus and speed let it snipe unescorted rams, mangonels and trebuchets.
units.look: Small light rider with no lance or armor, often alone near sheep or your base; faster than horsemen and has no shield.

units.name: Spearman
units.why: Large flat bonus vs anything tagged cavalry turns a 7-dmg hit into 24+. But it is light infantry: archers get +5 vs light melee infantry, MAA armor (3-5) cuts its 7-11 base hits, springald +12 vs melee infantry.
units.look: Foot soldier with long spear held upright or levelled, light cloth/leather; no big shield. Longer weapon than MAA, no plate.

units.name: Man-at-Arms
units.why: 4 ranged armor nearly nullifies 5-dmg arrows and 4 melee armor cuts spear hits. Crossbows deal +10 vs heavy, knights out-damage it and choose fights with speed, springald +12 vs melee infantry pierces lines.
units.look: Fully armored foot soldier with sword/mace and shield, metal helmet; stockier and slower than spearmen, no long pole weapon.

units.name: Archer
units.why: Fast fire rate and bonus vs light melee infantry shred spears. Low base damage (5) is wasted on 4 ranged armor (MAA, knights). Horsemen have 2 ranged armor and +9 vs ranged; mangonel +10 vs ranged in an area.
units.look: Unarmored foot unit with a short/recurve bow, quiver; lighter than crossbowmen (no stock weapon held horizontally).

units.name: Crossbowman
units.why: 11 + 10 bonus mostly ignores 4-5 armor, so heavy gold units melt. Slow reload means it wastes damage on cheap light units; 80 HP unarmored dies to horsemen (+9 vs ranged), mangonel splash, and cost-efficient archers.
units.look: Foot ranged with a crossbow held horizontally, often helmeted; slower shot cadence than archers. French version carries a pavise shield.

units.name: Handcannoneer
units.why: One 38 dmg shot minus 4-6 armor still deals 30+, so armor-based units lose. Short range (4), slow speed and no armor let horsemen (+bonus vs ranged) and splash siege (mangonel +10 vs ranged) punish it.
units.look: Foot soldier holding a tube gun; big smoke puff and loud bang on each shot; shorter range than archers.

units.name: Horseman
units.why: Fastest generic land unit with bonus vs ranged and siege and ranged armor vs arrows. Spearmen deal +17..+28 vs cavalry; knights/MAA out-armor and out-damage it head on.
units.look: Rider with light armor and a short spear/javelin, no lance couched, no plate barding; bigger than a scout, lighter than a knight.

units.name: Knight
units.why: 24 dmg + charge with 4/4 armor beats almost everything that lacks a cav bonus; arrows do 1-3 per hit. Spearmen get +23 vs cavalry at Veteran, crossbows +10 vs heavy, monks convert 240 resources of unit.
units.look: Heavily armored rider in plate on a large horse, sword or couched lance (Lancer); bulkier than horsemen, often barded horse.

units.name: Horse Archer
units.why: Range 4.5 and speed 1.625 out-move infantry (1.125-1.25). Archers out-range it (5) and are cheaper; horsemen are faster (1.875) with +ranged bonus; 85 HP unarmored dies to any focused ranged fire.
units.look: Unarmored rider shooting a bow while mounted; no lance, lighter horse than knights. Mongol Mangudai and Ayyubid Desert Raider look similar.

units.name: Monk
units.why: Conversion trades 150G for a 240-1000 resource unit; healing sustains gold armies. 90 HP, slow and no armor, so fast cavalry or focused archers kill it before it gets value.
units.look: Robed unit without weapons, often holding a book/staff or carrying a relic chest; slow and stays behind the army.

units.name: Imam
units.why: Identical logic to Monk: cheap conversion of expensive units; fragile 90 HP support.
units.look: Robed, turbaned support unit with no weapon, usually trailing the army or walking to relics.

units.name: Trader
units.why: Slow, unarmored and on predictable routes: light cavalry raids kill trade cheaply.
units.look: Cart or pack animal with a driver moving along a fixed route between markets/trade posts.

units.name: Springald
units.why: Long range piercing bolts with +12 vs melee infantry punish MAA/spear blobs. Only 85 HP: horsemen (+siege bonus) and knights dive it; cannons outrange and one-shot it.
units.look: Large wheeled crossbow (giant ballista) pushed by a crew; fires a single long bolt; smaller than a mangonel/trebuchet.

units.name: Mangonel
units.why: Splash plus +10 vs ranged one-volleys clumped 70-130 HP ranged units. Minimum range 3, setup time and 0.75 speed make it helpless vs cavalry diving it; gunpowder siege outranges it.
units.look: Wheeled torsion catapult with a throwing arm and bucket; lobbed rocks/fireballs splash on impact; bigger than springald.

units.name: Battering Ram
units.why: 95% ranged resistance makes towers, TC arrows and archers useless, but melee hits land fully, so villagers, spearmen, MAA and cavalry (+siege) kill rams quickly.
units.look: Covered wooden shed on wheels with a swinging log/iron ram head, slowly approaching buildings; infantry walk beside it.

units.name: Siege Tower
units.why: Near-immune to arrows (95% resist) but has no attack, so any melee unit kills it before it docks.
units.look: Tall wooden tower on wheels, much taller than a ram, rolling toward stone walls.

units.name: Counterweight Trebuchet
units.why: Range 16 outranges defenses, but it is inaccurate vs units, must pack/unpack and moves at 0.625: cavalry with +siege bonus kill it; cannons hit it from 10 range.
units.look: Very tall wooden frame with a long arm and hanging counterweight; huge slow lobbed stones; largest siege silhouette.

units.name: Bombard
units.why: Siege damage ignores armor/ranged resistance so it one- or two-shots enemy siege and buildings. Min range, setup and 0.75 speed make it cavalry food; culverins outrange it (10.5).
units.look: Huge black-iron gun barrel on a wooden sled/cradle, fired with big smoke; no wheels or very low carriage.

units.name: Culverin
units.why: Longest-range generic gun with fast reload: picks off other siege before it can fire. Like all siege it dies to cavalry diving it.
units.look: Long slender cannon on a two-wheeled carriage; longer and thinner barrel than bombard.

units.name: Cannon
units.why: Same logic as bombard: siege damage deletes buildings and siege, but needs escort vs cavalry.
units.look: Wheeled cannon on a field carriage (more mobile than bombard sled).

units.name: Ribauldequin
units.why: Multi-barrel volley kills clumped infantry and 10 melee armor shrugs off melee. Only 35% ranged resistance and range 3.75, so archers/crossbows and longer-range guns kill it.
units.look: Small cart with a rack of several thin gun barrels side by side (organ gun); short range smoke volley.

units.name: Fishing Boat

units.look: Small single-sail or rowed boat working near fish shoals or docks.

units.name: Trade Ship
units.why: Unarmed, predictable route.
units.look: Larger cargo ship without weapons travelling dock to trade post.

units.name: Archer Ship (Galley

counterRules.if: Enemy scout stealing sheep / harassing villagers in Dark Age
counterRules.build: Own scout to escort sheep; 1-2 spearmen if they commit horsemen
counterRules.why: Scouts deal +10 vs scouts and only 1 base damage, so your scout or any spearman/villager group wins.
counterRules.avoid: Chasing with villagers far from base

counterRules.if: Dark Age barracks with Vanguard MAA (English) or early spearman rush
counterRules.build: Palisade + archers in Feudal, garrison TC, towers/outposts; later own MAA
counterRules.why: Vanguard MAA have 3 ranged armor but only 100 HP; TC arrows, archers en masse and walls buy time until you match armor.
counterRules.avoid: Spearmen vs MAA (armor cuts their damage)

counterRules.if: Mass archers in Feudal (2+ archery ranges)
counterRules.build: Horsemen to flank; MAA if available; later mangonel
counterRules.why: Horsemen have 2 ranged armor and +9 vs ranged; MAA's 3-4 ranged armor reduces 5-dmg arrows to 1-2.
counterRules.avoid: Spearmen (archers get +5 vs light melee inf)

counterRules.if: Spearman + archer Feudal army (standard trash mix)
counterRules.build: Early MAA (if civ has) + archers, or archers + horsemen flanks
counterRules.why: MAA beats both: armor vs arrows and spears. Your own archers beat their spears; horsemen pick off archers.

counterRules.build: 2-4 spearmen at each resource, outposts/palisade, TC garrison bell
counterRules.why: Spearmen deal +17..+28 vs cavalry; raids need ranged-free, spear-free targets to pay off.

counterRules.if: Feudal knights (Rus Early Knights, French Royal Knights)
counterRules.build: Spearmen massed + archers behind; hurry to Castle for crossbows
counterRules.why: Spearmen's cavalry bonus ignores knight armor; archers do little vs 3-4 ranged armor so they need spears in front.

counterRules.build: Veteran spearmen + crossbowmen; monks/imams to convert
counterRules.why: Vet spear +23 vs cavalry, crossbow +10 vs heavy; conversion steals 240-resource units.
counterRules.avoid: Archers, horsemen, chasing with slow infantry in open

counterRules.build: Knights/lancers flanking crossbows + your own crossbows; mangonel or springald
counterRules.why: Knights kill 80 HP crossbows and out-trade MAA; your crossbows +10 vs MAA; mangonel splashes clumped crossbows, springald +12 vs MAA.

counterRules.build: Horsemen, mangonels, or cheap archers
counterRules.why: Crossbow bonus is wasted on light units; horsemen +bonus vs ranged; mangonel +10 vs ranged splash.
counterRules.avoid: MAA/knights walking in head-on without flank

counterRules.build: Crossbowmen, springalds behind a spear wall, knights; handcannons in Imperial
counterRules.why: Crossbow +10/+12 vs heavy, springald +12 vs melee infantry, knight 24 dmg; handcannon 38 dmg ignores armor.

counterRules.build: Archers (range 5 > 4.5) and horsemen; mangonel on their blob
counterRules.why: HA are unarmored, 85 HP; archers outrange and are cheaper; horsemen are faster (1.875 vs 1.625) with +ranged bonus.

counterRules.build: Spearmen (bonus vs elephants) + crossbowmen; monks/imams convert; bombards late
counterRules.why: Elephants are heavy and huge HP: spear elephant bonus and crossbow +heavy chew them; conversion swings 750+ res; bombard +50 vs war elephant.

counterRules.build: Crossbowmen + spearmen dive; mangonel or bombard
counterRules.why: High ranged armor (7) blunts archers; crossbow bonus vs heavy and spear elephant bonus still work.

counterRules.if: Feudal battering rams (Siege Engineering) at your TC/landmark
counterRules.build: Pull villagers or send spearmen/MAA/horsemen to melee the rams
counterRules.why: Rams have 95% ranged resistance but no melee protection; 370 HP (410 after 17.0) dies fast to melee.
counterRules.avoid: Relying on TC/tower arrows or archers

counterRules.build: Horsemen or knights flanking the siege; own bombards/culverins in Imperial
counterRules.why: Siege has 80-95% ranged resistance but horsemen get +siege bonus; setup time and min range make it helpless up close.

counterRules.build: Horsemen/knights dive springalds; culverin/bombard if Imperial
counterRules.why: Springald has 85 HP and 55% ranged resistance; cavalry with +siege bonus kills it, while its +12 bonus only hits infantry.
counterRules.avoid: Blobbing MAA/spears in front of it

counterRules.if: Mass mangonels behind a ranged army
counterRules.build: Spread your ranged, flank with horsemen/knights, counter-mangonel or bombard
counterRules.why: Mangonel splash +10 vs ranged erases clumped archers; its 3 min range and setup let cavalry kill it.

counterRules.build: Cavalry dive with Biology; culverins (10.5 range) to outrange; springald on bombards rarely enough
counterRules.why: Gunpowder siege has 85% ranged resistance and 190-215 HP; melee cavalry and longer-range guns win.

counterRules.build: Archers/crossbows from range, mangonel or culverin
counterRules.why: Ribauldequin has range 3.75, only 35% ranged resistance but 10 melee armor: shoot it, don't melee it.
counterRules.avoid: Massed infantry or melee cavalry charging in

counterRules.build: Horsemen (Elite), mangonels, ribauldequins
counterRules.why: HC: 130 HP, no armor, range 4 and slow; horsemen +13 vs ranged, splash siege kills clumped HC.
counterRules.avoid: MAA/knights walking into a HC line

counterRules.build: Horsemen to snipe monks; grab relics with your own monks
counterRules.why: Monks have 90 HP and no attack; relics in a monastery give steady gold all game.
counterRules.avoid: Ignoring relics on an open map

counterRules.if: Monks in army converting your knights/elephants
counterRules.build: Light cavalry to kill monks; spread expensive units; cheaper trash
counterRules.why: Conversion steals the costliest unit in range; horsemen are fast enough to reach backline monks.

counterRules.build: Pull villagers to kill builders, spearmen/MAA; relocate eco; later springald/ram
counterRules.why: Unfinished towers die to villagers; finished ones need melee siege or rams (95% ranged resist).

counterRules.if: 1 TC, no military buildings, early Castle landmark (fast Castle)
counterRules.build: Feudal aggression: horsemen/archer raids, MAA + rams, or take map control and boom
counterRules.why: A fast Castle player is under-armed for 3-5 minutes; punish eco or take free resources.
counterRules.avoid: Passive play that lets them hit Castle units first

counterRules.build: Early pressure: horsemen raids, archer+spear push, Feudal rams
counterRules.why: TCs cost 400W 300S and 150 s (165 s in 17.0); damage before payback wins.

counterRules.build: Springald ships (Hulk/Baghlah/War Junk)
counterRules.why: Springald ships get +45 vs archer ships and have 3 ranged armor.

counterRules.build: Archer ships screen; spread fleet
counterRules.why: Archer ships deal +18 vs fire ships; incendiaries have 145 HP.

counterRules.build: Incendiary ships, shore bombards/trebs/springalds
counterRules.why: 'Massive' ships take +300 from incendiaries; bombard +410, treb +200, springald +65 vs ships.

counterRules.if: Late game: enemy all-gold army (knights, MAA, HC) and gold mines running low
counterRules.build: Trash: spearmen + archers + horsemen with full upgrades; save gold for siege/upgrades
counterRules.why: Spear bonus vs cav and archers vs light units cost no gold; trade efficiently as their gold dries up.
counterRules.avoid: Matching gold-for-gold when out of gold

counterRules.if: Late game: enemy mass trash (spears, archers, horsemen)
counterRules.build: MAA + knights, mangonel/springald/ribauldequin support, full armor upgrades
counterRules.why: Armor upgrades make 5-11 dmg trash hits worthless; splash siege deletes clumps.

counterRules.build: Trebuchets/bombards, or rams/siege towers with infantry; raid elsewhere
counterRules.why: Trebs outrange keeps (16); rams +300 vs walls; walls are passive so take the map meanwhile.

limitations: Reads only what the HUD shows; nothing hidden by the fog of war.
Frames are sampled every few seconds, so very short idle periods can be missed.
HUD positions and the civilisation list are researched, not yet checked against live captures at every UI scale.
Mistake durations are measured in real time on your screen.
The villager curve assumes a 20-second villager and the usual six-villager start; some civilisations differ, and villagers lost to raids also show as a gap.

Fights are followed from frames where your army is fighting on screen; a fight off screen is missed. The outcome combines how the fight looked with your army size (population minus villagers), so fights where neither is clear are logged as unclear, not called.
failClosed: No cloud vision: this pack cannot read the game.
Numbers that cannot be read are left out, so no mistake is counted while the HUD is hidden or blurry.
